correctness.rationale: For a uniform vertex in a fixed retained subgraph, the j-th raw component-size moment is n^{-1} times the sum of component sizes to power j+1. When the independently retained new edge joins components of sizes a,b, the conditional increments for j=1,2 are 2ab/n and 3ab(a+b)/n; otherwise both vanish. Calling their expectations A and B gives a mean increase pA and a variance change p(B-2 mu_G A)-p^2 A^2. The all-closed state proves A>0 for every interior p and supplies the leading values mu_G=1, A=2/n and B=6/n with O(p) errors, giving the coefficient 2/n in the variance change. In every merging state a+b<=n, so B<=3nA/2 and mu_G>=3n/4 yields strict negativity even at equality via -p^2 A^2. Connectedness gives mu_G tending to n, and polynomial continuity gives a crossover, not uniqueness. The threshold uses the original graph's mean; the variance averages over both seed and bonds.
residual_risks: The reported 12,908 finite comparisons were not independently replayed; the proof, not that sweep, supplies the universal quantifiers.
No extension to nonuniform seeds, directed graphs, or dependent or heterogeneous transmissions is asserted.

value.rationale: The statement resolves a natural question that mean monotonicity does not answer: the same single graph edit has opposite signs on unconditional variance at the two ends of a common bond parameter. The original-graph mean alone gives a usable simultaneous sufficient test for all nonedges, without comparing their entire distributions. The variance theorem, not the elementary mean observation or tiny example alone, is the contribution.
residual_risks: No optimality of the threshold or uniqueness of a crossover; neither the graph result nor a decrease in variance alone establishes a change in real-world harm.
